successors.note: Assigned to German East Africa on 1 July 1890, a military post in 1896, forced into the treaty of Ikiganda in 1902-1903; Belgian forces occupied Gitega on 17 June 1916 and the monarchy 'surrendered ten days later'; Ruanda-Urundi mandate 20 July 1922; independence as a monarchy 1 July 1962; republic 28 November 1966.

capitals.note: The infobox lists Gitega and Bujumbura; the page dates no capital for the kingdom. The German seat moved from Usumbura to Gitega in 1912.

ledger.note: 1902-1903: Mwezi IV is forced into the treaty of Ikiganda. 'Resident Friedrich Robert von Beringe and the anti-king Kilima attacked Mwezi IV, who was forced into the treaty of Ikiganda' (the page, 1902-1903); Burundi had been assigned to German East Africa on 1 July 1890. The year 1903 and the loss of sovereignty are the researcher's reading of the treaty.

sources.title: Kingdom of Burundi
sources.note: Founding c. 1680, Ntare IV conquests c. 1795-1852, borders by 1850, Mwezi IV 1852-1908, 1 July 1890 assigned to German East Africa, 1902-1903 treaty of Ikiganda, Belgian occupation 17 June 1916, republic 28 November 1966.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has the Republic of Burundi from 1963 only). One page: Kingdom of Burundi. It names no territory but 'modern Burundi' and the divided kingdom of Bugesera; its kings are Ntare I (c. 1680-1705), Ntare IV (c. 1795-1852) and Mwezi IV (1852-1908), with the other reigns missing from the extract, so no ruler strip is given.

Not on the page: conquests of Buyenzi, Kirimiro and Bweru, wars with Rwanda as such, the Muramvya capital, the 1903 treaty's terms (the page says 'treaty of Ikiganda' and does not mention Gisabo). The end year 1903 is the researcher's reading of the Ikiganda treaty; the monarchy ended in 1966.

Counterparts needing dossiers: german-africa (af-08), the kingdoms conquered under Ntare IV (none), Bugesera (none), Rumaliza's Arab domain (af-06 might hold it). Gazetteer names needed: Bugesera, Kirimiro.
